QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_21

question.text: Category I and Category II AIFs can invest a maximum of what percentage of AUM or investable funds in a single investee company?

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.5: Cat I and Cat II AIFs cannot invest more than 25% of AUM or investable funds in a single investee company (directly or via AIF units). The Trap: Option A is the Cat III limit. Option C is wrong. Option D exceeds the rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests this Cat I/II cap; XIX-C requires monitoring across drawdowns. Manager's Pro-Tip: Because Cat I/II invest in illiquid unlisted companies, the 25% limit is computed on INVESTABLE FUNDS (not NAV) — this is more GP-friendly but LPs sometimes misread. Always footnote the denominator in LP reports.
